newsitem.title: USA: Ringer expects sales to rise this year.
newsitem.headline: Ringer expects sales to rise this year.

text.p: Ringer Corp said Friday it expected sales to rise by 20 percent to 25 percent this year and was searching for acquisition opportunities.

"While we still have the fourth quarter ahead of us, we expect sales for the year to be approximately 20 percent to 25 percent higher than last year," Stanley Goldberg, chairman and chief executive said. "In addition we would expect our balance sheet to remain strong, our cash flow to be at about break even and operating results consistent with last year."
Earlier Ringer said it earned $184 million, or $0.02 a share, in the third quarter ended June 30 compared with $105,000, or $0.01 a share, in the same period last year.
In April Ringer acquired Dexol Industries Inc, a California maker and marketer of pesticides for the homeowner market, for an undisclosed amount.

"While our first priority is to effectively integrate Dexol, we are continuing to actively identify and evaluate a number of acquisition opportunities," Godlberg said. "We believe the acquisition of Dexol, coupled with the financing package we secured from GE Capital Services, now puts Ringer in a position to build a larger, stronger and a more financially sound company."
